name: Application Programming Interface (API) Security Requirements Guide
description: This Security Requirements Guide is published as a tool to improve the security of Department of Defense (DOD) information systems. The requirements are derived from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) 800-53 and related documents. Comments or proposed revisions to this document should be sent via email to the following address: disa.stig_spt@mail.mil.

rules.title: The API must encrypt data in transit.
The API must be configured to use approved authorizations for access control.
The API must enable monitoring and alerts.
The API Gateway must generate audit records when successful/unsuccessful attempts to access privileges occur.
The API must generate audit records when successful/unsuccessful attempts to access privileges occur.
The API Gateway must generate audit records of what type of events occurred.
The API must monitor the usage of API keys to detect any anomalies.
The API must generate audit records of what type of events occurred.
The API must audit rate-limiting events.
The API Gateway must audit rate limiting events.
The API Gateway must audit authentication and authorization information.
The API must audit authentication and authorization information.
The API Gateway must audit exceptions and errors that occur during the processing.
The API must audit exceptions and errors that occur during the processing.
The API Gateway must audit execution time and performance metrics.
The API must audit execution time and performance metrics.
The API Gateway must audit request and response details (such as method, URL, headers, body, status, etc.).
The API must audit request and response details (such as method, URL, headers, body, status, etc.).
All defined API elements must be documented.
API keys must be configured with usage restrictions.
The API must limit the exposure of endpoints.

The API must use an approved DOD enterprise identity, credential, and access management (ICAM) solution to uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users (or processes acting on behalf of organizational users).
The API must protect Session IDs via encryption.
The API keys must be securely generated using a FIPS-validated Random Number Generator (RNG).
The API implementation must use FIPS-validated encryption and hashing algorithms to protect the confidentiality and integrity of API keys.
The API must encrypt sensitive cached data.
The API must employ throttling.
The API must specify allowed origins when using Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS).
The API must not disclose sensitive data in error messages.
Access to API privileged features and functions must be restricted.
The API must require periodic reauthentication.
The API must have a mechanism for cache invalidation when using cache policy data.
When stateless authentication tokens are used, the API must configure them with appropriate security settings.
The API's internal authorization tokens must not be provided back to the user.
API access tokens must be configured to expire.
API refresh tokens must be configured to expire.
The API must enforce per-client rate limits.
Clients must be configured to route requests through a single API gateway that enforces the association and transmission of organization-defined security attributes with each request.
The API must use a gateway.
The amount of data returned by the API must be restricted.
The API must use TLS version 1.2 at a minimum.
The API must audience-restrict access tokens in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must use parameterized queries.
The API must provide input validation.
The API must authenticate remote commands.
The API must encode outputs.
The API must use a static type of system.
The API must use Web Application Firewall (WAF).
The API must use a FIPS-validated cryptographic module to provision digital signatures for tokens.
API services identified within the system as unnecessary and/or nonsecure must be disabled.
The API must provide protected storage for API keys.
API must use a circuit breaker pattern to handle failures and timeouts.
Cryptographic keys that protect access tokens must be protected.
The API must protect the private keys used to sign assertions and tokens.
Generating assertions must be restricted.
The API must issue assertions in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must refresh assertions in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must revoke assertions in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must time-restrict assertions in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must audience-restrict assertions in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must generate access tokens in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must issue access tokens in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must refresh access tokens in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must revoke access tokens in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
The API must time-restrict access tokens in accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy.
